claims.text: The starting material is an as-processed Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy with a non-equilibrium, metastable solid-solution-plus-intermetallic state.
Eutectic solidification can overcome performance limitations associated with stable intermetallic formation in Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloys.
Eutectic solidification produces a near-equilibrium microstructure.
The eutectic microstructure has low-energy phase boundaries.
The eutectic microstructure has regular lamellar organization.
Near-equilibrium eutectic microstructures resist microstructural change at high temperatures up to their reaction temperature.
The eutectic microstructure provides high rupture strength.
Eutectic solidification improves room-temperature compressive behavior relative to the as-processed baseline.
Eutectic solidification improves corrosion resistance relative to the as-processed baseline.
Eutectic solidification improves resistance to high-temperature oxidation relative to the as-processed baseline.
The applicable temperature boundary extends up to the eutectic reaction temperature.

contradictions.description: The initial material is described as a non-equilibrium, metastable solid-solution-plus-intermetallic state, whereas the baseline is described as having stable intermetallic formation; the relationship between the metastable initial state and the allegedly stable intermetallic baseline is not resolved.
